subject: Clarify: subprocessor blacklist, tenant output ownership & no-training path
messages:
From: Elena Rivera <elena.rivera@healthsuite.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.example>
Cc: data-privacy@healthsuite.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA questions: no-training, subprocessors, and exportability

Hi David,

Quick note from our legal/privacy team — HealthSuite is reviewing the latest DPA and we have three asks we need to validate before procurement can sign:

1) No-training commitment: we need an enforceable clause that our tenant traffic will not be used to improve models or be retained for model training. Is that a standard option?

2) Subprocessor blacklist: we need a way to exclude specific subprocessors (for example, onshore GPU providers in certain countries) from processing HealthSuite data. Can you share how Redwood handles a customer blacklist and what evidence you can provide?

3) Cross-border exportability: for EU/UK data we sometimes require documented routing and proof of where model inference and KV caches run. Do you have a simple exportability statement and recent evidence for EU residency or fallback routing?

If helpful, I can share a short list of subprocessors we are worried about. Attaching our DPA change request doc.

Thanks — Elena

Attachment: HealthSuite-DPA-change-request.docx (docx, 42 KB)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.example>
To: Elena Rivera <elena.rivera@healthsuite.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.example>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions: no-training, subprocessors, and exportability

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and then a proposed next step: 

- No-training: yes, we offer a "model improvement opt-out" for paid customers. It includes a contractual no-training clause plus an ops-side routing and KV cache policy to prevent tenant data from being captured for upstream training.

- Subprocessor blacklist: we support customer blacklists for specific subprocessors at contract time. Practically that means we will: 1) refuse to route your traffic to blacklisted entities, and 2) provide an inventory and attestations showing routing/region. For certain on-demand cloud providers we may offer a dedicated pool option as a fallback.

- Exportability/evidence: we can provide an exported inventory and a short residency statement (where inference executes, KV cache residency, and audit logs). We also have per-route model-variant fallbacks if a region is unavailable.

What I need from you: the specific subprocessors/regions you want blocked, and whether you require KMS onshore or a dedicated pool. I attached our current preliminary subprocessor inventory to speed things up.

Proposed next step: loop Legal + Privacy so we can return a contract redline + a one-page operational runbook (routing, cache controls, evidence items) within 3 business days. Does that timeline work?

Regards,
David Kim
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: preliminary-subprocessor-inventory.csv (csv, 14 KB)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.example>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.example>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA questions: no-training, subprocessors, and exportability

Fwd-ing HealthSuite's asks. Key asks: enforceable no-training clause, customer subprocessor blacklist, and proof of where inference/KV caches run for exportability.

My read / suggestions:
- Legal: propose a short clause: "Provider will not use Customer Data to improve, train, or benchmark models, and will segregate Customer Data from model training pipelines; any deviation requires Customer's prior written consent." Keep it contract-light but enforceable (audit right + termination on breach).

- Privacy: produce an ops-runbook that covers: routing policy (by region + route priority), KV cache retention (ephemeral by default, per-customer TTL), and audit log export steps.

- Ops (Dev): confirm how quickly we can provide a signed attestation and a CSV on residency for a given tenant, and if we can guarantee that traffic will never touch a given subprocessor via routing tables / deny-lists.

If Legal is OK with the clause, I'll propose it back to the customer and offer a Dedicated fallback (reserved GPU pool) if they insist on blocking major cloud providers. Attaching the DPA starter I typically propose.

Thanks — David

Attachment: redwood-dpa-draft.pdf (pdf, 96 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.example>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.example>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA questions: no-training, subprocessors, and exportability

Thanks for the context. Draft clause below and proposed action items. Please review and call out any operational gaps.

Draft clause (suggested insertion into Section 3 - Data Processing):
"Provider shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, improve, or benchmark Provider models, nor shall Provider retain Customer Data for those purposes. Provider will maintain logical and operational controls (including but not limited to routing deny-lists, tenant-scoped KV cache TTLs, and dedicated pooling where requested) to implement the foregoing. Provider will allow Customer to: (i) identify subprocessors to be excluded from processing Customer Data; (ii) request attestations and export logs evidencing routing and residency. Breach of this clause shall be a material breach entitling Customer to injunctive relief and termination rights."

Action items:
- Ops (Dev): produce a template attestation + CSV export for HealthSuite within 48 hours. Include service logs that show region/model variant routing and KV cache residency.
- Privacy (Kimberly): review the clause and confirm if we should add an audit-window (e.g., quarterly attestations or on-demand with NDA).
- Sales (David): offer Dedicated reserved pool pricing as an alternative if customer blacklists two or more of our primary cloud partners.

Timeline: aim to return to HealthSuite with the redline + runbook + attestation within 3 business days.

Marissa
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

P.S. We should avoid absolute "never" language without a remediation path; the above balances contractual protection with operational realities.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.example>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA questions: no-training, subprocessors, and exportability

David / team — quick notes on operational feasibility and evidence we can provide.

1) Attestation and CSV: we can produce a signed attestation (Legal + Security) and a per-tenant CSV that maps routing decisions to subprocessors and regions for the last 90 days. We will mark KV cache nodes and model-variant instances in the CSV.

2) Deny-lists / routing: our routing layer supports deny-lists at the tenant level; we can implement a blacklist within 48-72 hours but for certain ephemeral on-demand providers the only guaranteed path is a Dedicated pool. The deny-list blocks routing but doesn't control operator-level access if the provider is used for other tenants — that's why Dedicated is recommended for absolute isolation.

3) KMS / key residency: we can support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) in supported regions. If HealthSuite needs onshore KMS for EU/UK data, we'll need to confirm which cloud partner they'd accept.

Operational ask for HealthSuite: provide the list of subprocessors and whether they require onshore KMS. We'll then prepare the attestation and a sample CSV.

Kimberly
Head of Privacy, Redwood Inference

Attachment: none
